clue.text: Sweet female, one with little depth, likely to be nicknamed Chubby Chops?

definitions.text: likely to be nicknamed Chubby Chops?

parts.note: a pudding is a sweet course
an ace is the one in a suit of cards
d is the abbreviation for depth, so a little of it

explanation.surface: A sweet girl, not very deep, whom people might tease as Chubby Chops.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet here is the British word for dessert, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a round, plump face, like a pudding, would draw a teasing nickname about fat cheeks.

clue.text: RC clergy work in endlessly troublesome dark times (12, two words, apostrophe)

indicators.note: the work goes inside the shortened word
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: pesky means troublesome
op is short for opus, a work
nights are the dark hours

explanation.surface: Catholic priests working through grim, dangerous years.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope's knight was an old jocular name for a Roman Catholic priest, from the courtesy title Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was a jibe at Catholic priests as servants of Rome given knightly titles.

clue.text: Bituminous mineral got from earth with bits of yellow and liard in colour

indicators.note: these letters go inside the word for colour

parts.note: dye is a colour
sod is turf cut from the earth
the first letter of yellow
the first letter of liard, an old word for grey; bits of covers both colours

explanation.surface: A mineral dug from the ground, flecked yellow and grey.
explanation.walkthrough: Liard is an archaic word for grey, so the surface is a mineral in two colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysodyle is a foul-smelling lignite or paper coal that burns with a bituminous odour.

clue.text: It's stupid for Scots to make life abroad

parts.note: to do is to make
vie is French for life

explanation.surface: It's daft, say the Scots, to make a life overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dovie is a Scots adjective meaning dull-witted or stupid.

clue.text: Poet relating to central life system

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Gérard de ..., French Romantic poet
second meaning: an adjective for the nerves

explanation.walkthrough: The nervous system is the central life system here.
explanation.definitionFit: The French writer's surname is also a rare adjective for things concerning the nervous system.

clue.text: Hiring a cart? It can possibly be this? It can

definitions.text: Hiring a cart? It can possibly be this? It can

indicators.note: possibly means the letters can be rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
these letters are what is left over beyond the answer

explanation.surface: Wondering whether hiring a cart is a feasible idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of it can out of hiring a cart and the rest rearrange into an Indian hired carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gharri is a horse-drawn carriage hired out in India, so hiring a cart describes it.

clue.text: Athletic fellows on time for trying on of kit?

indicators.note: in a down clue the earlier pieces sit on top of the letter for time

parts.note: athletic people are fit
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Sporty men turning up on time for a kit fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitment can mean the act of fitting, as when a tailor fits clothes on someone.

clue.text: One bit of lettuce with egg on high table?

indicators.note: takes the first letter of lettuce

parts.note: first letter of lettuce
to tar on is an old phrase meaning to urge or incite

explanation.surface: A lettuce leaf and an egg served at a college high table.
explanation.walkthrough: High table suggests a college dinner, but the answer is the raised table in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The altar is the raised table at the east end of a church, set high for worship.

clue.text: What's hidden by schemers eventually rising to the surface

indicators.note: the answer sits concealed inside the following words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of schemers and the start of eventually

explanation.surface: A plotters' secret that eventually comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: Emerse is a botanical adjective for leaves standing above the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes plant parts that stand out above the water surface.

clue.text: Languished with great waves splitting head in state of poor health

indicators.note: the waves go into the middle of the word for languished

parts.note: died, as in faded away
seas are heavy waves
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Someone wasting away, with huge breakers beating on the headland, in poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A diseased condition is a sick state, hence the abstract noun for ill health.

clue.text: 'Once upon a time', having nothing in front around start of yarn (6, two words)

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: the front word goes around the next letter

parts.note: fore means at the front

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of yarn

parts.note: first letter of yarn

explanation.surface: A storyteller's opening line, with nothing before the yarn begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are fairy-tale formulas for a long-ago past, so the archaic expression matches the storybook opening.

clue.text: Diplomats are economical with the truth? It's madness

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, home of British diplomats
a famous euphemism for telling lies

explanation.surface: A dig that diplomatic spin is insane.
explanation.walkthrough: Economical with the truth was a notorious civil-service phrase from a British court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Folie is French for madness, used in English phrases such as folie à deux.

clue.text: Scar starts to hurt if left untreated medically

indicators.note: the opening letter of each following word is taken in turn

parts.note: the first letters of these five words spell the answer

explanation.surface: A wound left unseen by a doctor may scar.
explanation.walkthrough: The hilum is the scar on a seed where it was joined to its stalk, a botanical sense far from the medical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use the term for the mark left on a seed coat at its point of attachment.

clue.text: Tumult aplenty right in scenes of conflict

definitions.note: a plural answer, fair because aplenty asks for many tumults rather than one

indicators.note: the letter for right is placed inside the other word

parts.note: battles are where conflicts are fought

explanation.surface: Battlefields full of noisy uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: A brattle is a Scots word for a clattering din; aplenty asks for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Each brattle is a loud rattling uproar, so several of them make plenty of tumult.

clue.text: Take away disused oriental cut of meat

parts.note: E for East
loin is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: A takeaway of an old eastern meat dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Disused flags an archaic word; this one comes from legal French.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to remove or carry off, now obsolete, hence the warning that it is out of use.

clue.text: Top man in hôtel de ville, one in very awkward situation

definitions.text: Top man in hôtel de ville

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the other word

parts.note: being in the mire is being in deep trouble

explanation.surface: The mayor at the town hall finds himself in a real fix.
explanation.walkthrough: A hôtel de ville is a French town hall, so its top man is the French mayor.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for mayor names the civic head who presides at the town hall.

clue.text: Cider as mixed in cocktail

indicators.note: the letters are stirred together into a new order, as drinks are mixed

explanation.surface: Cider mixed into a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice, served in a cocktail glass.

clue.text: Innkeeper upended sherry barrel of highest quality

indicators.note: the sherry and barrel letters are stood on end, read upwards

parts.note: fino is a pale dry sherry
ace means first-rate

explanation.surface: A landlord tips up a cask of the finest sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: Boniface is the landlord in Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem, and his name came to mean any innkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a stage landlord became a general literary term for a publican.

clue.text: To more than one such … there's free use of Skype (a lot)?

definitions.text: To more than one such … there's free use of Skype (a lot)?

indicators.note: making free with the letters means they may be rearranged at will

parts.note: taken as written
the first letter of lot
S is the plural ending, marking more than one

explanation.surface: People with several online pen friends make heavy use of free Skype calls.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters spell the plural, which is what more than one such asks for; take away that plural S and the singular entry is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A keypal is a pen friend you correspond with by email or over the internet, so such calls suit them.

clue.text: Exterminate, Dalek-style? Doctor to me is following answer

indicators.note: the doctored letters come after the answer
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A Doctor Who scene: the Dalek's threat, with the Doctor as foe.
explanation.walkthrough: Daleks, the Doctor Who villains, shout Exterminate and zap victims with ray guns.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast something to atoms is the sci-fi way of destroying it utterly, as a Dalek would.

clue.text: Reveals, e.g. to Hebridean, what's gone wrong in island

definitions.note: the Scots word for the reveal of a door or window

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the abbreviation
gone wrong means the letters of gone are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something has gone amiss on a Scottish island, and someone is disclosing it.
explanation.walkthrough: Reveals is a noun: the side faces of a window or door opening. The Hebrides are Scottish islands, so the word is Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots an ingo is the inner side surface of a door or window recess, what builders call a reveal.

clue.text: They may be ploughing on silt

definitions.text: They may be ploughing on silt

indicators.note: ploughing turns over soil, so the letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Farmers working the rich silt of a river valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Nile peoples farm the silt the floods leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilots are peoples of the Nile valley, whose farming depends on the river's fertile mud.

clue.text: Tangle that is enveloping dysfunctional clan

indicators.note: the abbreviation wraps around the jumbled letters
the letters of clan are put out of order

explanation.surface: A family feud: a broken clan caught in a tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To inlace is to lace or entwine together, so to entangle.

clue.text: Dug well, something done half-heartedly?

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring or well

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters is lost

parts.note: a deed is something done

explanation.surface: Someone dug a well, though without much enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To spade ground is to turn it over with a spade, which is digging.

clue.text: Point of view lacking in lawsuit

indicators.note: without the word in, which is taken out

parts.note: instance is an old legal term for a suit or its process

explanation.surface: A legal case with no clear perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: Instance in its legal sense means a lawsuit, as in a court of first instance.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is the attitude or position someone takes on a question.

clue.text: Clarinet's symmetrically placed pieces in unaccompanied part for wind

indicators.note: these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a solo is a part played alone
the third letter from each end of clarinet

explanation.surface: A clarinettist with a solo part for a wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Wind is the weather, not woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The solano is a hot, dusty easterly wind of south-east Spain.

clue.text: Peak (sort of) cloudy on ascent

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: c stands for cloudy in the Beaufort weather notation
a rise is an ascent

explanation.surface: A mountain top wrapped in cloud as you climb.
explanation.walkthrough: Crise is an old form of crisis; a crisis is a turning point or climax, which is a peak of a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is the decisive culminating point of an illness or affair, hence a kind of climax.

clue.text: Roll up when one's entering for bran derivative

indicators.note: the letter for one goes into the other word

parts.note: to furl is to roll up a sail or flag
one is a; it is the letter that goes in

explanation.surface: An invitation to step up for a bran product.
explanation.walkthrough: Fural is short for furfural, an oil distilled from bran, whose Latin name is furfur.
explanation.definitionFit: Furfural, shortened to fural, is an aldehyde made chemically from bran and husks.

clue.text: NZ honey guide, backward weakling, fed by boy nervously

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside, as food goes into a mouth
the word for the weakling is written in reverse

parts.note: a drip is a feeble, wet person

indicators.note: the letters of boy jitter into a new order

explanation.surface: A timid lad guiding someone to honey in New Zealand.
explanation.walkthrough: The poy-bird, or poe-bird, is another name for the tui, a New Zealand honeyeater.
explanation.definitionFit: The tui is a nectar-feeding songbird of New Zealand, known locally by this alternative name.

clue.text: Complexion lost? Delete milk

parts.note: blee is an obsolete word for complexion or colour
D is the proofreader's short form of dele, delete

explanation.surface: Someone loses their colour and cuts milk from their diet.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed someone is to drain or exploit them, just as you milk them for money.

clue.text: Like type of rock, uranium-laden, the Scots seize

indicators.note: the uranium symbol is loaded inside the word

parts.note: glam rock is a style of 1970s rock music

explanation.surface: Scots grab a radioactive mineral specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock is music here, not stone: glam rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaum is a Scots verb meaning to snatch or clutch at something.

clue.text: Butterfly in pastel finery

indicators.note: the letters run within these two words

parts.note: the answer spans the end of pastel and the start of finery

explanation.surface: A butterfly dressed in soft-coloured splendour.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfins are small North American butterflies of the hairstreak family.

clue.text: Shrew, tough one, about first in rant and invective

indicators.note: the word for tough goes around the two initials

parts.note: hard means tough

indicators.note: first in picks out the opening letter, here of rant and of invective

parts.note: the first letter of rant
the first letter of invective too, first in covering both words
an means one

explanation.surface: A shrewish woman, tough and given to ranting abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrew is the scolding woman, not the small mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, scolding old woman, the same type as a shrew.

clue.text: Quarry in which a seam is revealed

indicators.note: the letters show within the run of words

parts.note: the answer runs from the end of which through a into seam

explanation.surface: A stone quarry where a seam of mineral comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarry is the hunted animal, not a stone pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The chase can mean the creature being hunted, which is also what quarry means.

clue.text: Part of pope's family, nameless scattering incense

indicators.note: scattering the letters gives a new arrangement

parts.note: without N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An anonymous relative of the pope swinging a censer.
explanation.walkthrough: Popes were known for advancing nephews and nieces, the origin of nepotism.
explanation.definitionFit: A pope's sisters' and brothers' daughters were part of the papal family he notoriously favoured.

clue.text: Beer cook kept in dresser, bolted? There are fixed opening times for such (12, two words)

definitions.text: There are fixed opening times for such

indicators.note: these letters are placed within the others
the letters of dresser run off in a new order

parts.note: ale is beer
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A cook hides beer in the kitchen dresser, then runs off; the pub has set opening hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Fixed opening times points to pubs, but it is the moment a sealed instruction may be opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealed orders are instructions that must not be opened until a stated time or place.
